clue.text: It is brought back into service by eastern artist

indicators.note: into says the turned piece goes inside the word for service

parts.note: Mass is the church service of the Eucharist

indicators.note: brought back says the word it is to be read in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written, then turned

explanation.surface: Some item is restored to working order by a man from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses the pronoun and 'into' sets it inside the church service; 'by' is only a link joining the eastern letter on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was the French painter famed for Fauvism and paper cut-outs, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Disable sound for musical

indicators.note: sound tells the solver the word for disable is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to maim is to disable or cripple

explanation.surface: An instruction to mute the volume, as on a television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disable sound' reads like switching off the audio; in fact 'sound' signals that the synonym MAIM is heard, spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Mame is a Broadway show by Jerry Herman about the eccentric Auntie Mame, so an example of a musical.

clue.text: Mormon's end by salt lake

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, as is a tar

indicators.note: end picks out the final letter of the Mormon's word

explanation.surface: A Mormon's death beside the Great Salt Lake in Utah.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer order is TAR then N: 'by' simply sets the two pieces side by side. 'salt lake' looks like one phrase, but salt is the sailor and lake alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, especially in the Lake District of northern England.

clue.text: Is £25 raised in two seconds for summary?

indicators.note: in places the turned-up pieces between the two letters

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, so two seconds give two Ss

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, means the pieces are read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: Asking whether a sum of money can be collected almost instantly, by way of a brief recap.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' means read upwards, so the pieces are reversed before 'in' puts them between the two seconds. A pony as £25 is British money slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A synopsis is a brief outline giving the gist of a longer work, a synonym for a summary.

clue.text: Official source of berries

definitions.meaning: a senior officer of a church or tribe, an official

explanation.definitionFit: Elder is both a church official and the shrub whose dark fruit are elderberries.

clue.text: Part of flower that's right in wrong place

indicators.note: in tells the solver the letter for right goes inside the rearranged word
wrong, as in placed wrongly, means the letters of place are disordered

explanation.surface: A botanical part that is correct but sits in an incorrect position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges PLACE to CAPEL, and 'in' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpel is the female reproductive organ of a flower, holding ovary, style and stigma, so one part of it.

clue.text: Go away with a very small relative

parts.note: V is the abbreviation, the shortened form, of very
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Leaving with a tiny member of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' here means shortened: very in small is V. 'very small relative' reads as a tiny cousin.
explanation.definitionFit: Avaunt is an archaic exclamation meaning begone, an old command telling someone to leave.

clue.text: Expert testimony ousting leader in state capital

parts.note: a pro, short for professional, is an expert

indicators.note: ousting leader means the first letter of the word is thrown out

parts.note: evidence is testimony given in court

explanation.surface: A specialist witness's account pushing aside the head of a regional government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousting leader' turns EVIDENCE into VIDENCE. 'Expert testimony' reads as one legal phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence is the capital city of Rhode Island, so an example of a US state capital.

clue.text: A final note about a fabulous writer

indicators.note: about, as in moved about, means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A last musical note concerning a wonderful author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but rearranges A FINAL NOTE. 'fabulous' is a pun: the writer wrote fables.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean de La Fontaine wrote the celebrated French Fables, making him literally a writer of fables.

clue.text: Girl keeps desperate chap back to prepare food

indicators.note: keeps says the girl's name holds the other piece within it

parts.note: Marie is a girl's name

indicators.note: back says the chap's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a strongman in the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A young woman looks after a down-and-out man in order to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is the cow-pie-eating strongman of the British children's comic The Dandy; 'back' reverses his name before the girl 'keeps' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To marinade meat is to steep it in seasoned liquid before cooking, one way to prepare food.

clue.text: Fuss about rolled gold remote

indicators.note: about says the word for fuss goes around the other piece

parts.note: to faff is British slang for fussing about ineffectually

indicators.note: rolled, as in rolled over, means the word for gold is turned backwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A commotion over a sheet of gold that has been rolled up, far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled gold' reads as a jewellery term, but 'rolled' reverses the heraldic gold and 'about' puts the British slang for fuss around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere far-off is distant, a close synonym for remote.

clue.text: Party clobber

definitions.meaning: British slang for a lively party

explanation.definitionFit: Thrash is informal for a wild party, and as a verb means beat soundly, as clobber does.

clue.text: Dread being caught

definitions.meaning: being caught is arrest by the police

explanation.definitionFit: Apprehension means anxious fear, and also the capture of a suspect by the police.

clue.text: Observation post initially set in place on the other side

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letters of the two words

parts.note: to position something is to set it in place

explanation.surface: An army lookout is first put on the far side of the lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observation post' reads as a military phrase; take only its initials. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics or sport the opposition is the opposing party or team, the other side.

clue.text: Youngster gets hit on the head before producing original work

indicators.note: before puts the word for hitting on the head ahead of the youngster

parts.note: to brain someone is to hit them on the head
a child is a youngster

explanation.surface: A child is struck on the head before creating something new.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainchild is someone's own original idea or invention, a creative product of their mind.

clue.text: Nice point

definitions.meaning: nice in its old sense means fussy or precise
a point is a single detail or item

explanation.definitionFit: Particular means fastidious, the old sense of nice, and as a noun a detail or point.

clue.text: Get out of bed for our top bananas?

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go mad and rearrange

explanation.surface: Asking whether rising in the morning is the right thing for our best people, who are going mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get out of bed' sounds like waking up; it means pulling a plant out of a flower bed. 'top bananas' reads as 'chief people'.
explanation.definitionFit: To uproot is to pull a plant out of the ground, a garden bed in this case.

clue.text: Extremely eloquent, a letter for Ephesians

indicators.note: extremely picks out the outermost letters of the word

explanation.surface: A very articulate epistle written to the church at Ephesus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter for Ephesians' suggests Paul's epistle; it means a letter of the Greek alphabet that the Ephesians wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet, the alphabet used in ancient Ephesus.

clue.text: Early riser's first to go — pretended to go out with terrier

indicators.note: out with says the word for pretended goes around the trimmed word

parts.note: a sham is a pretence, so a pretended thing

indicators.note: to go says a letter must leave the word early
first picks the opening letter of the riser's word

explanation.surface: A dog that pretended to go out early, before its owner got up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riser's first to go' drops the R of early; 'out with' has the word for pretended go round what is left. A Sealyham is a Welsh terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sealyham is a small white Welsh breed of terrier, so an example of the dog.

clue.text: Japanese band leaders in Osaka being inscrutable

indicators.note: leaders in means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A Japanese music group whose frontmen in Osaka are impossible to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests a music group; it is a sash.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is the broad sash worn around a kimono, literally a band of cloth.

clue.text: Clergyman once had car converted

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A priest who used to own a car that was then modified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' also suits religion, which hides that it rearranges ONCE HAD CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdeacon is a senior Anglican cleric ranking below a bishop, an example of a clergyman.

clue.text: Additional accommodation in which queen gets to kiss sweetheart

parts.note: Anne was a Queen of Great Britain
X is the cross signing a kiss at the end of a letter
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A guest room where the queen gets to kiss her beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' reads as a lover but means the heart of 'sweet', its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extra building attached to a main one, often for extra rooms or guests.

clue.text: Deeply distressed, blowing up nice balloons

indicators.note: blowing up means exploding, so the letters are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone heartbroken as pleasant balloons are being inflated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing up' seems to go with balloons, but it rearranges NICE BALLOONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inconsolable cannot be comforted, being so deeply upset.

clue.text: A set of points in mint condition

parts.note: S, N, E and W are the four points of the compass

explanation.surface: A collection of scores for a newly minted item.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass points are S, N, E and W, here in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something as new looks unused, the same as being in mint condition.

clue.text: Sea creature old record label depicts

parts.note: RCA is a famous American record company

explanation.surface: A whale painted on the sleeve of a vintage record.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca, or killer whale, is a large black and white marine mammal.

clue.text: Witnesses going up and down

indicators.note: going up and down says the word reads the same in both directions of the down light

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Observers moving up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: To see something happen is to witness it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: One grows flowers

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
something that rises grows or increases

explanation.surface: A gardener who raises blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are plants with showy, often blue or purple flowers.

clue.text: Responsible for reaching wreck

indicators.note: wreck means to ruin, so the letters are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Being to blame for getting to a shipwreck.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in charge of something is to be responsible for it.

clue.text: Refusal day after day, then editor indicated acceptance

parts.note: no is a refusal
D is the abbreviation for day, twice

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor who kept saying no, then finally agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who nodded moved their head down and up as a sign of agreement or acceptance.

clue.text: An outgoing woman crazy for marsupials

indicators.note: outgoing means the letters leave the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
bats is British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A sociable lady who is mad about kangaroo-like animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outgoing' looks like 'sociable' but removes AN from WOMAN, leaving WOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Wombats are burrowing Australian marsupials that carry their young in a pouch.
